$comment: Topics, `topic slug -> { doorway, ccc, documents, canons, lead }`, merged into the shipped
index by scripts/sync-corpus.mjs and read by /quaestiones and /quaestiones/{slug}.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A FIELD IN the corpus's build/*/manifest.json: the reason
descriptions.json and document-tags.json each give. Those manifests are GENERATED, a re-parse
rewrites them, and this project fixes parsers by re-parsing. A topic is editorial -- it is
somebody's judgement that a reader's question is answered HERE -- so it lives in tracked
source and is merged in on the way to the site.
WHAT A TOPIC IS NOT: it is not a subject. `site/document-tags.json` holds the subjects, and
they are browse axes over documents -- `labour`, `ecclesiology` -- chosen so a facet row
partitions the document set. Nobody arrives at a facet. They arrive at `my father died`, or
`I cannot stop`, or `is my first marriage still binding`, and docs/research/topics.md is the
pass that worked out the difference. The four DOORWAYS below are that finding: the argument
(tribal, public, googled mid-fight), the life event (something happened on Tuesday), the
private shame (2 a.m., and they would never ask a person) and the ordinary question.
THE ANCHOR IS A CATECHISM SPAN, AND THE PASSAGES ARE NOT CHOSEN HERE. That is the whole
posture of the file. CCC 2357 already carries `Gen 19:1-29; Rom 1:24-27; 1 Cor 6:10;
1 Tim 1:10` and `CDF, Persona humana 8` in its own footnotes, and ProseBlocks linkifies them
wherever that paragraph is rendered -- so naming the span gets the Scripture and the
magisterial citation for free, chosen by the Catechism rather than by us. Where the span is
one of the Catechism's OWN headings (`Chastity and homosexuality` is `[2357, 2359]` in
build/ccc.en/structure.json) the editorial act is smaller still: the topic IS the heading.
`documents` and `canons` carry what the Catechism's footnotes do not reach -- a document
written after the CCC, or a procedure the Code holds and the Catechism only names. They are
additions to the derived set, never a replacement for it.
`lead` IS THE ONE REAL JUDGEMENT IN THIS FILE, and it is one field wide so it can be argued
with. A span renders in paragraph order unless `lead` names a paragraph to put first. It is
needed because the Catechism's order is systematic and a reader in trouble is not: CCC
2280-2283 opens on the gravity of suicide and closes on `We should not despair of the eternal
salvation of persons who have taken their own lives`, and a bereaved mother served those four
paragraphs in printed order meets three she cannot bear before the one she came for. Same for
2357 before 2358, and for the reader who has already had the abortion.
This is closer to editorialising than anything else on the site does, and it was taken
deliberately (2026-09-09, by direction) on the ground that the alternative is not neutrality:
printed order is itself an ordering, chosen by someone else for a reader who is not this one.
NOTHING IS OMITTED BY IT -- `lead` reorders a span and never trims one, so the paragraph a
reader is spared first is still on the page.
SLUGS ARE LATIN, like every other address here, and where the Catechism has its own word for
the thing the slug takes it -- `divinatio` is CCC 2116's, checkable against ccc.la. An address
names the same topic in every language and takes no interface prefix, which is the
distinction site/docs/addresses.md rests on; an English slug would quietly make English the
language the site is addressed in.
THE WORD `quaestio` NOW MEANS TWO THINGS ON THIS SITE and that is known, not overlooked
(2026-09-09, by direction). `/doctores/summa/{part}` addresses the Summa's quaestiones, which
are a unit of a text somebody else wrote; these are a reader's questions, which are ours. The
copy on both pages names its own sense rather than relying on the word.
THE VOCABULARY OF DOORWAYS IS CLOSED, and sync-corpus.mjs exits 1 on a topic outside it, on a
CCC span naming a paragraph this build has not got, on a document slug naming no document, on
a canon this build has not got, and on a `lead` outside its own topic's spans. The last is the
one worth stating: a `lead` that has drifted out of its span is invisible on the page, because
a page that silently renders in printed order looks exactly like a page nobody wrote a `lead`
for.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT is recorded in docs/research/topics.md: a topic the corpus cannot
answer properly does not ship. Addiction has CCC 2290-2291 and nothing else; yoga waits on
`Orationis Formas`; the Latin Mass on `Traditionis Custodes`; same-sex blessings on `Fiducia
Supplicans`, which is the worst of them, since the three earlier documents ARE here and a
stale answer reads exactly like a current one. Adding a topic is a deliberate act -- it is a
claim that a reader asking this will be better served than not asking.
THE TITLES AND THE QUESTIONS ARE NOT HERE. They are prose a reader reads, so they are
`quaestiones.{slug}.*` in the i18n dictionaries like every other word of chrome, and until all
thirty-seven carry them this route stays out of CHROME_PATHS on route-manifest.ts's own terms.
